According to the latest IDC report, although Mac shipments fell 11% in Q3 2026, Apple's market share rose from 8.5% to 9.5% because overall market shipments plunged 20.1%. Here are the details.

In a challenging environment, Apple outperformed most of the PC market

IDC today released its global PC shipment report for Q3 2026, noting that although Mac shipments decreased compared to last year, Apple clearly outperformed the overall market.

According to IDC's preliminary data, Apple shipped 5.9 million Macs in Q3 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million in the same period last year.

However, the overall PC market declined even more sharply, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-over-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

Apple therefore maintained fourth place, behind Lenovo. Lenovo led the way with 14.9 million shipments and a 23.8% share, followed by HP with 10.3 million shipments and 16.5%, and Dell in third with 7.6 million shipments and 12.1%.

Among the top five vendors, HP saw the largest year-over-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. ASUS had the smallest decline, down 8.6% year-over-year, with shipments of 5.5 million units and a market share of 8.7%.

IDC said:

Looking ahead, IDC noted that "concerns among channels about weak demand amid high inventory and high prices could drive promotional activity in the near term," and added that "pricing will remain well above prior-year levels."

The firm also said the economy has weakened since last quarter, which could further weigh on demand and make "the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027 even darker."
